name: Destroyer Droid
instructions: omr/instructions/8002-1-1.pdf (scan of both books: book 1 is pages 2-35, the legs and lower body, with its function shown on pages 31-35; book 2 is pages 36-98, the rest, with the change into a wheel shown on pages 85-98; pages 99-130 build an alternate model)

functions.does: The droid changes from its standing attack shape into a wheel: the curved brown shell, hinged to the top of the back, swings forward and down round the body, while the arms, head and legs fold in, until it is a ball that can be rolled along the floor.
functions.source: book: photos on pages 85-96 and the four small pictures on page 98
functions.note: the shell is the model's frame (body 0 holds the shell, its sensor arm and the tail), so the control is the body, turning against the shell on the two hinges at the top of the back; how far it swings, and what stops it, isn't shown

functions.does: The head on the front end of the shell, with its red-tipped sensors, folds down against the body.
Each arm swings in at the shoulder, folding its twin blasters against the body for rolling, and out again to aim.
functions.source: book: photos on pages 88-90; inferred: which way each arm turns

functions.does: Each twin blaster bends at the elbow of its arm.
functions.source: inferred: arm steps on pages 71-83 hinge the blasters on long pins; the book doesn't show it moving

functions.does: The two front legs fold back under the body for rolling and swing down to stand on.
functions.source: book: photo on page 87; inferred: that the two legs fold together on one hinge

functions.does: The single back leg swings up over the back to close the wheel, and down again to stand on.
functions.note: the back leg hangs from the body on two hinges and is linked to the shell's lower ends (tail submodel), so it may swing as the shell does: unsure

functions.does: Pressing the red pin on top of the shell pushes a rod down the middle that frees a catch, and a rubber band snaps the back leg up; pulling the pin up resets it. In book 1, before the shell is built, the red trigger under the back does the same.
functions.source: book: photos on pages 31-35 and 92-95; plunger rod in book 2 (axle 10 down the middle)
functions.skip: the catch and the rubber band only matter under force; the pin itself slides down and up, as a push

functions.does: Catches click to hold the arms and the shell folded in the wheel shape, and rubber bands spring the droid open again into its attack shape when it's set down.
functions.source: book: photos on pages 89, 91 and 97 (clicks drawn); book 1 steps 7, 10, 25 and 34 (rubber bands)
functions.skip: catches and rubber bands only matter under force

functions.does: In the wheel shape the droid rolls along the floor on the rim of its shell.
functions.skip: rolling the whole model on its shell needs gravity
